name: cx-goal-one-rule~p2
task: Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Open the door, then pick up the box in the other room.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The first clause asserts a global Absence of `key_lost`. The task only requires that the agent try not to drop the key while the door is still closed, i.e., avoid a `key_lost` event when `door_open` is false. A global Absence prohibits any key loss, even when the door is open, which is not stated in the task. Replace the clause with a soft Absence of `key_lost` conditioned on `!door_open` (or a soft constraint that penalizes `key_lost` when the door is closed). The remaining hard clauses (`Existence(door_open)`, `Existence(target_picked_up)`, `Precedence(door_open,target_picked_up)`) correctly capture the rest of the task.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task says "Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed." This is a preference that only applies to dropping the key when the door is closed. The clause uses soft Absence(key_lost), which forbids the key_lost event at any time (including after the door is open). This misrepresents the task. Replace the clause with a soft rule that only penalises key_lost when door_open is false, e.g., a soft Absence(key_lost) conditioned on !door_open, or a soft Response(door_open, ~key_lost) that allows dropping the key only after the door is open. The other clauses (Existence(door_open), Existence(target_picked_up), Precedence(door_open,target_picked_up)) correctly capture the remaining requirements.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The first clause misrepresents the task’s instruction "Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed." The task specifies a soft avoidance of the event `key_lost` occurring when `door_open` is false (i.e., while the door remains closed). The compiler clause is a soft `Response(door_open, key_lost)`, which actually forces every time the door opens that `key_lost` must occur afterwards—a requirement opposite to the task wording. Replace the first clause with a rule that forbids `key_lost` while `door_open` is false (e.g., a soft `Absence(key_lost)` under the condition `!door_open` or a custom rule equivalent). All other clauses correctly capture the hard goals and order.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The soft Absence(key_lost) clause forces the agent to never drop the key at any time. The task only requests a soft preference to avoid dropping the key while the door is closed; dropping the key after the door is open is acceptable. Therefore this clause over‑restricts the allowed behavior. Remove or relax this clause (e.g., keep it only as a preference that penalizes key_lost but does not forbid it outright).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The first clause asserts a soft Absence(key_lost), i.e. that the agent should never drop the key. The task, however, only requires avoiding key_lost *while the door is still closed*. By enforcing Absence(key_lost) everywhere, the clause over‑specifies the task and adds a constraint that is not mentioned in the text. Remove this clause or replace it with a conditional rule that forbids key_lost only when door_open is false.

texts: The agent should avoid dropping the key while the door remains closed (soft preference).
The agent must eventually open the door.
The agent must eventually pick up the target box.
The door must be opened before the target box is picked up.
